clue.text: Daily, for example, reversal of cost

parts.note: a daily is a cleaning woman, a char

indicators.note: a reversal turns the preceding abbreviation round so it is read from its end

parts.note: the usual abbreviation for 'for example'

explanation.surface: A newspaper such as the Daily something has reversed its cover price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily, for example' reads as one idea, a newspaper, but a daily is also a British term for a cleaner who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge is to ask a price, so as a noun a charge is the price or fee asked.

clue.text: Caught dealer, one who trades in wicked goods

definitions.text: one who trades in wicked goods

parts.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a handler deals in stolen goods

explanation.surface: A dealer in criminal merchandise has been arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked goods' sounds villainous but means goods with wicks: candles, which a chandler sells.
explanation.definitionFit: A chandler originally made and sold candles, which have wicks, hence the playful phrase for his merchandise.

clue.text: A school lecturer brewed strong drinks

indicators.note: brewing mixes and transforms ingredients, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: A teacher at a school has been making potent home brew.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcohols, in the sense of spirits and other intoxicating beverages, are strong drinks.

clue.text: Dull elegist by the sounds of it

indicators.note: the phrase says we are going on what is heard, not how the word is spelt

parts.note: Thomas Gray wrote the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard

explanation.surface: A writer of elegies seems rather dreary from what people say.
explanation.walkthrough: The elegist is Thomas Gray, whose surname is said exactly like the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey describes something dull and cheerless, lacking colour or interest.

clue.text: Hot air from gentleman accepting compliance with companies going back and forth

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the title word holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: the title for a gentleman
C stands in loosely for compliance, as in the C of a compliance mark

indicators.note: moving in both directions means the abbreviation is written backwards then forwards

parts.note: CO for company, written once reversed and once forwards

explanation.surface: Pompous talk from a businessman over firms dithering about following the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: C slips into SIR after its first letter, then CO for company appears reversed and forwards. 'Hot air' looks like windbag talk but is literal: the hot desert wind.
explanation.definitionFit: The scirocco is a hot, dusty Mediterranean wind blowing from North Africa, quite literally hot moving air.

clue.text: Small boy in audition goes over lines randomly

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the name is taken by its sound only

parts.note: Chris, a boy's name and a shortened Christopher
to go over a road is to cross it, the verb here in its third person form

explanation.surface: A little lad trying out for a part skims the script haphazardly.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly 'goes over' together gives the crossing; the sound of the boy's name supplies the first half.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisscross is a pattern of lines crossing one another in many directions, so plural crisscrosses are lines laid haphazardly.

clue.text: Shops aired dismally romantic pieces of music

indicators.note: done dismally means done badly, so the letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Stores played sentimental tunes over their speakers to poor effect.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhapsody is a free, emotional single-movement composition, typical of the Romantic era.

clue.text: Old boxer's manager gained zero

indicators.note: gaining something here means taking it inside, so the round figure is put within the other word

parts.note: a coper is one who copes, someone who manages
the round shape of zero

explanation.surface: A retired fighter's agent ended up with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Cooper was a much-loved British heavyweight of the 1960s; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Henry Cooper, British heavyweight champion who famously floored Cassius Clay, is the boxer meant.

clue.text: Should a vegetable grower know his well?

definitions.text: Should a vegetable grower know his well?

parts.words: Should a vegetable grower know his well?
parts.note: surface reading: a question about whether a gardener ought to understand his crops
setter's reading: the idiom 'know one's ...' for being expert, completed by a bulb vegetable

explanation.walkthrough: To know your onions is British idiom for knowing your subject thoroughly; a vegetable grower might be expected to know them literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for expertise names this pungent bulb, which a grower would literally need to understand.

clue.text: Tell, say, when demonstrator loses his head

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a demonstrator on a protest march

explanation.surface: A protester is beheaded, and we are told to report it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell' is not a verb here but William Tell, the Swiss marksman who shot an apple off his son's head.
explanation.definitionFit: William Tell is the legendary Swiss bowman, an example of a skilled shooter with bow or crossbow.

clue.text: Baltic city into cooking pasta

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the small word beside it is rearranged

parts.note: the capital of Latvia
these four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone from Latvia's capital has taken up making pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' looks like a connecting preposition but is the material to be cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigatoni are ridged tubes, one of the standard Italian pasta shapes.

clue.text: Pro establishment bringing jam round at 4

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so the jam word wraps the rest

parts.note: a conserve is a fruit jam
taken as written
four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone backing the system brings preserves round at four for tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The jam surrounds the pair AT plus Roman four, sitting before its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: A conservative favours existing institutions and traditional order, i.e. supports the status quo.

clue.text: Boy reflected about hot Indian food

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the boy word reads the other way
about means around, so the reversed word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: a lad is a boy
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A young man thinks about spicy Indian cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Dahl, or dal, is a South Asian dish of stewed lentils or split pulses.

clue.text: Gents maybe endlessly promiscuous

indicators.note: without its end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: loose in its old sense of sexually unrestrained

explanation.surface: Men, perhaps, who sleep around without limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gents' reads as men, but it is the British name for a men's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gents is British slang for a men's lavatory, an example of a loo.

clue.text: Prominent scientist, not a German mug

indicators.note: not means without, so the following German word is taken away

parts.note: Albert Einstein, the physicist
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: A famous scientist, who was not a German fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mug' suggests a dupe, but it is the drinking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A stein is a large earthenware beer mug, often lidded, of German origin.

clue.text: Insisted Democrat worked on Southern rebels

indicators.note: something worked has been shaped and reshaped, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for Democrat
S for southern

explanation.surface: A Democrat insisted on lobbying Southern rebels.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissidents oppose official policy or the ruling regime, so they are rebels against authority.

clue.text: Sweet treats served by London hide-outs

parts.note: EC, the postcode of the City of London
a lair is a hiding place

explanation.surface: Cakes are on offer at secret London dens.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postcode for the City of London district.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclairs are cream-filled choux pastries topped with chocolate, a classic sweet treat.

clue.text: Actor Paul, who played a little role, getting the red-eye

definitions.text: Actor Paul, who played a little role
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the American actor who played Ant-Man, a tiny hero
second meaning: a freshwater fish also called the red-eye

explanation.walkthrough: 'A little role' sounds like a bit part but is a tiny superhero; 'red-eye' suggests a night flight but is the fish's other name.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Rudd is the Ant-Man star, and the rudd is a European freshwater fish known for its red eyes.

clue.text: Grocers intrinsically backing sustainability label

indicators.note: going backwards means the hidden letters are read right to left
intrinsically means within, so the letters are found inside the word

parts.note: the middle three letters of the shop word

explanation.surface: Shopkeepers at heart support green labelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Eco is a prefix and label marking products as environmentally friendly.

clue.text: Troubled attendee unable to take a bite

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An anxious guest at the dinner cannot eat anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentate means toothless, and with no teeth one cannot bite.

clue.text: Tanning ex-PM in government

parts.note: Gordon Brown, UK Prime Minister 2007-10
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: A former premier is getting a suntan while in office.
explanation.definitionFit: Browning the skin in the sun is the same as tanning it.

clue.text: Emperor overwhelmed by part of Soviets' army

indicators.note: the answer is swallowed up inside a portion of the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A Russian ruler is overthrown by a Red Army unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsar was the emperor of Russia before the 1917 revolution.

clue.text: Prodigal son to hang former head of state

parts.note: S for son, as in genealogies
to pend is to hang, as in pendulum
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: The prodigal son's story ends with a call to execute a deposed ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prodigal son' looks like one phrase from the parable; only the first word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A prodigal is a wastrel who spends money recklessly, so a heavy spender; the adjective also works as noun.

clue.text: Dandy left inside joint

indicators.note: inside places the abbreviation within the dandy word

parts.note: a spiff is a smartly dressed man
L for left

explanation.surface: A fop has gone off into a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' reads as a venue, but it is a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A spliff is slang for a hand-rolled cannabis cigarette, also called a joint.

clue.text: Senior servant still essentially alert

parts.note: still in the sense of nevertheless

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letters are kept

parts.note: the three letters at the heart of the word

explanation.surface: An elderly retainer remains watchful at heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The butler is the chief manservant of a household, in charge of the others.

clue.text: Small lake surrounds university enclosure

indicators.note: surrounding means going all round, so the water word holds the letter

parts.note: a pond is a small body of still water
U for university

explanation.surface: A little lake rings a campus enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A pound is a pen or enclosure for stray animals or impounded vehicles.

clue.text: Summit of Twitter these days following Apple regularly

indicators.note: the social media letter is placed after the fruit letters, which it follows
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters
Twitter was renamed X in 2023

explanation.surface: The top people at Twitter now trail behind Apple.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point, the peak of a mountain.

clue.text: Downfall of some nepotistic old world leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their opening letters

parts.note: initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Some favouritism-ridden old leaders around the world were toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downfall' seems to mean ruin, but read literally it is something that falls down from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow is a fall of precipitation, so a snowfall is literally a downfall from the clouds.

clue.text: Lady singer out to lunch

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the American pop star known as Lady ...
second meaning: slang for crazy or not with it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady singer' looks like a female vocalist but is the stage name Lady Gaga.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga is both the second part of the pop star's name and slang for being senile or dotty.

clue.text: Unwell in old island state

parts.note: ill means unwell
taken as written
O for old
IS for island, as on maps

explanation.surface: Someone falls sick on an ancient island.
explanation.definitionFit: Illinois is a Midwestern US state whose largest city is Chicago.

clue.text: Expedition from South Africa to remote India

parts.note: the country's abbreviation
far means distant
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A trip goes from South Africa to far-off India.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an overland expedition, especially to observe or hunt wild animals in Africa.

clue.text: Woodman in favour of new trees

indicators.note: making something new means remaking it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: for means in support of
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A lumberjack argues for planting fresh trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A forester manages and works in woodland, as a woodman does.

clue.text: Scoundrel ordered gallon after gallon

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, to order
G for gallon
a second gallon, placed after the first

explanation.surface: A rogue asks for one gallon after another at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like an anagram signal but is simply the past tense bade.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad egg is an idiom for a dishonest or untrustworthy person.
